content.prompt: Convert $63\text{ km/h}$ to metres per second.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{speed}&=\frac{63\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}\\\text{speed}&=\frac{(63\times1000)\text{ m}}{(1\times60\times60)\text{ s}}\\\text{speed}&=17.5\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Convert $22\text{ m/s}$ to kilometres per hour.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{speed}&=\frac{22\text{ m}}{1\text{ s}}\\\text{speed}&=\frac{(22\div1000)\text{ km}}{(1\div60\div60)\text{ h}}\\\text{speed}&=79.2\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
A car had a full tank of 64 L at the start of a 280 km journey.
At the end of the journey, the fuel tank was three eighths full.
How much fuel was used on the journey?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Fuel left}&=\frac{3}{8}\times64\\\text{Fuel left}&=24\text{ L}\\\text{Fuel used}&=64-24\\\text{Fuel used}&=40\text{ L}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
A Ballarat factory has 4 identical machines packing boxes of apples.
Each machine packs 90 boxes every 3 hours.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the combined rate of the 4 machines, in boxes per hour.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Rate of one machine}&=\frac{90}{3}=30\text{ boxes/hour}\\\text{Combined rate}&=4\times30\\\text{Combined rate}&=120\text{ boxes/hour}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How long will the 4 machines take to pack 840 boxes?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Time}&=\frac{840\text{ boxes}}{120\text{ boxes/hour}}\\\text{Time}&=7\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

sourceAtom.label: Example
sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Find an average rate of change

inlines.text: A tree grows from 80 cm to 140 cm tall over 5 years.

inlines.latex: \begin{align*}\text{Change}&=140-80=60\text{ cm}\\\text{Time}&=5\text{ years}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{60\text{ cm}}{5\text{ years}}\\&=\frac{60\text{ cm}\,\color{#ef6068}{\div5}}{5\text{ years}\,\color{#ef6068}{\div5}}\\&=\frac{12\text{ cm}}{1\text{ year}}\\&=12\text{ cm/year}\end{align*}

content.prompt: Find the average rate of change in each situation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A puppy weighs 4 kg at 2 months old and 10 kg at 8 months old. Find the average increase in mass per month.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=10-4=6\text{ kg}\\\text{Time}&=8-2=6\text{ months}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{6\text{ kg}}{6\text{ months}}=1\text{ kg/month}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The temperature was $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 3 pm and $13^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 6 pm. Find the average decrease in temperature per hour.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=25-13=12^\circ\mathrm{C}\\\text{Time}&=6-3=3\text{ hours}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{12^\circ\mathrm{C}}{3\text{ hours}}=4^\circ\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{hour}\end{align*}$$
See parts.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}7{:}45\text{ am to }12{:}45\text{ pm}&=5\text{ h}\\12{:}45\text{ pm to }3{:}15\text{ pm}&=2\text{ h }30\text{ min}\\\text{Total}&=7\text{ h }30\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: A 2 kg bag of rice costs \$5.60. A shop wants to sell a 5 kg bag of the same rice at the same value.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the cost of 1 kg of rice in the 2 kg bag.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Cost per kg}&=\frac{\$5.60}{2\text{ kg}}\\&=\frac{\$5.60\,{\color{#ef6068}\div2}}{2\text{ kg}\,{\color{#ef6068}\div2}}\\&=\$2.80/\text{kg}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What must the cost of 1 kg be in the 5 kg bag to give the same value?

answer.worked: Equal value means equal unit prices, so the 5 kg bag must also cost $\$2.80/\text{kg}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What should the 5 kg bag cost?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Cost of 5 kg}&=\$2.80/\text{kg}\times5\text{ kg}\\&=\$14.00\end{align*}$$

payloads.replacement:
**Simplifying** a rate means writing it as a **unit rate**: a rate whose second quantity is 1 unit.

1. Write the rate as a fraction with units.
2. Divide both quantities by the numerical value of the denominator.
  You can do this by entering the fraction in a calculator.
3. Write the simplified rate using the slash (/).

To convert a rate:

1. Write the rate as a fraction with units.
  The numerator is the first quantity and the denominator is 1 unit of the second quantity.
2. Convert each quantity to the required unit.
3. Simplify the fraction using a calculator.

The **best buy** is the option with the lowest price for each unit of the same quantity (for example, \$ per kg).

1. Convert both rates to the same units if they differ.
2. Simplify each to a unit rate in \$ per unit.
3. The lowest price per unit is the best buy.

We can solve rates problems by writing two **equivalent rates** as an equation. Equivalent rates describe the same relationship between two quantities, so they are equal.

1. Write the given rate as a fraction, then write an equal fraction using the new quantity. Let the quantity you want to find be $x$. Put the same quantity on top in both fractions and the same quantity on the bottom in both.
2. Solve for $x$.
3. If $x$ is in the denominator, take the reciprocal of both sides first.

content.prompt: In each case, find who has the higher rate, and by how much.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Mia types 450 words in 5 minutes. Liam types 1000 words in 8 minutes.

answer.worked:
Mia:
$$\frac{450\text{ words}}{5\text{ min}}=\frac{90\text{ words}}{1\text{ min}}=90\text{ words/min}$$
Liam:
$$\frac{1000\text{ words}}{8\text{ min}}=\frac{125\text{ words}}{1\text{ min}}=125\text{ words/min}$$
Difference:
$$125-90=35$$
Liam types faster by $35\text{ words/min}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Tank A fills with 1260 L of water in 7 hours. Tank B fills with 1500 L of water in 8 hours.

answer.worked:
Tank A:
$$\frac{1260\text{ L}}{7\text{ h}}=\frac{180\text{ L}}{1\text{ h}}=180\text{ L/h}$$
Tank B:
$$\frac{1500\text{ L}}{8\text{ h}}=\frac{187.5\text{ L}}{1\text{ h}}=187.5\text{ L/h}$$
Difference:
$$187.5-180=7.5$$
Tank B fills faster by $7.5\text{ L/h}$.

classification.difficultyReason: Compute two unit rates, then compare them and find the difference. Numbers are clean, and the 'higher rate and by how much' framing needs a little interpretation.

content.prompt: Give each answer to 2 decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A courier in Perth starts deliveries at 8:20 am and finishes at 5:20 pm. She delivers 50 parcels. Find the rate at which she delivers, in parcels/hour.

answer.worked:
From 8:20 am to 5:20 pm is $9$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rate}&=\frac{50\text{ parcels}}{9\text{ hours}}\\&=\frac{\frac{50}{9}\text{ parcels}}{1\text{ hour}}\\&\approx5.56\text{ parcels/hour}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A bushwalker leaves a campsite at 6:40 am and reaches a lookout at 1:40 pm after walking 25 km. Find her average speed, in km/hour.

answer.worked:
From 6:40 am to 1:40 pm is $7$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rate}&=\frac{25\text{ km}}{7\text{ hours}}\\&=\frac{\frac{25}{7}\text{ km}}{1\text{ hour}}\\&\approx3.57\text{ km/hour}\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Same demand as the Dr Rosanna question: find the elapsed time from the clock times, then divide and round to 2 d.p. The two parts repeat it.

content.prompt:
The conversion rate for New Zealand dollars (NZ\$) to Australian dollars (A\$) is $1.08\text{ NZ\}}/\text{A\$.
How many Australian dollars would I receive for NZ\$2700?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1.08\text{ NZ\}}}{1\text{ A\}&=\frac{2700\text{ NZ\}}}{x\text{ A\}\end{align*}$$

Take the reciprocal of both sides.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ A\}}}{1.08\text{ NZ\}&=\frac{x\text{ A\}}}{2700\text{ NZ\}\\x&=\frac{2700}{1.08}\\x&=2500\end{align*}$$

A\$2500

classification.difficultyReason: A single scaling step, but the rate is given as NZ$ per A$. The student must read its direction and divide, not multiply.

content.prompt:
Five identical pumps are used to drain a flooded car park in Geelong.
Each pump removes 180 L of water every 6 minutes.
How long will the 5 pumps take to remove 6000 L of water?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Rate of one pump}&=\frac{180\text{ L}}{6\text{ min}}=30\text{ L/min}\\\text{Combined rate}&=5\times30=150\text{ L/min}\\\text{Time}&=\frac{6000\text{ L}}{150\text{ L/min}}\\&=40\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Three linked steps: the per-pump rate, the combined rate for 5 pumps, then the time to remove 6000 L. Nothing is signposted, but all the steps are routine.
